_comment: Running handoff doc 01 for the Epic 10 W4 SIT fix-and-close cycle. Use this after runtime diagnosis confirmed that backend/runtime services are healthy but index.html parity/content is still broken on SIT.
title: Fix W4 SIT runtime parity/content issues, redeploy, and close with live proof
lane: Copilot - implementation plus deploy plus runtime closeout
objective: Finish the W4 SIT issue end to end. Apply the minimal Git fix needed to repair src/frontend/index.html parity and content integrity without breaking /phase2/prototype, strengthen the verification gate to catch false-positive deploy passes, redeploy through the Openclaw control-plane workflow, and return live runtime proof that both routes behave correctly.

mandatory_process.procedure: Procedure A - Deploy Code Change, followed by Procedure C style runtime verification if anything looks inconsistent
non_negotiables: No direct VPS modifications outside the approved Git plus GitHub Actions path
Implement the fix in Git first, then redeploy through Openclaw only
Do not stop at diagnosis or source-file proof; this task is complete only with live runtime verification
If new runtime inconsistency appears after deploy, inspect logs and runtime evidence before proposing another code pass

confirmed_runtime_truths: SIT containers and backend dependencies are healthy enough to serve requests
/phase2/prototype is the real production-facing W4 surface
/index.html is still stale or content-corrupted and does not match accepted W4 parity expectations
This is not primarily a backend outage
repo_truths_to_preserve: main-ux-ui.html already contains the real export/configurator wiring
Quick Export uses the backend null-template path
Configurator 3-tab shell plus real editor exists on main-ux-ui.html

what_to_do: 1. Confirm exactly how src/frontend/index.html differs from src/frontend/main-ux-ui.html in the W4-critical areas. Focus on mojibake, stale text, stale Quick Export fallback logic, missing configurator editor markers, and any content-integrity issue that can confuse SIT review.
2. Apply the minimal safe Git fix so index.html no longer contradicts the accepted W4 surface. Preserve the known-good /phase2/prototype behavior while repairing index parity and clean UTF-8 content.
3. Remove or replace any remaining stale index-side content that still implies client-side-only Quick Export or pre-W4 configurator behavior.

4. Add a lightweight verification guard that would have caught this false-positive deploy. This can be a focused check or script that validates shipped HTML body integrity/parity markers on both src/frontend/main-ux-ui.html and src/frontend/index.html.
5. Run focused local checks before deploy. At minimum: parse/structure checks for edited HTML and the smallest relevant test/check for the new guard.
6. Commit the fix on the intended branch if your workflow requires it, then trigger the Openclaw SIT deploy workflow against the correct ref.
7. After deploy, perform live runtime verification on both /phase2/prototype and /index.html. Use browser/runtime proof, not source-line proof only.
8. Confirm that the final result is good enough to close this SIT issue. If anything remains open, state the exact residual blocker and whether it is W4-blocking or only follow-up cleanup.

must_fix_or_verify.name: index.html parity and encoding/content integrity
must_fix_or_verify.expectation: index.html no longer shows mojibake or stale W4 UX and does not contradict main-ux-ui.html in the accepted review path intent

must_fix_or_verify.name: No stale Quick Export fallback messaging on shipped review surfaces
must_fix_or_verify.expectation: Shipped surface does not imply client-side-only Quick Export behavior if runtime path is backend-driven

must_fix_or_verify.name: Configurator parity markers
must_fix_or_verify.expectation: index.html contains current W4 configurator/editor markers needed for parity review and does not lag behind the latest accepted shell

must_fix_or_verify.name: Guard against future false-positive deploy pass
must_fix_or_verify.expectation: A focused verification step exists for body integrity/parity markers, not only route reachability or source markers

focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.name: phase2 runtime health
focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.expectation: /phase2/prototype loads with readable content and no blocker-level console or network errors

focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.name: index runtime parity
focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.expectation: /index.html loads with readable UTF-8 content and does not show stale pre-W4 export/configurator UX

focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.name: Quick Export runtime wiring
focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.expectation: Quick Export preview/download still call backend endpoints with null-template runtime columns after the parity fix

focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.name: Template Export runtime wiring
focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.expectation: Template Export preview/download still reflect per-run column_overrides

focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.name: Configurator clickability
focused_live_checks_after_redeploy.expectation: Configurator tabs and key actions remain clickable on the production-facing surface after redeploy

if_deploy_or_runtime_fails_check_in_this: Openclaw workflow run summary and first failing step
Evidence logs generated by the workflow
Browser console and failed network requests on the live routes
Whether the new parity/body-integrity guard would have predicted the failure
acceptance_criteria: The Git fix is minimal and targeted at the actual parity/content problem, not a broad unrelated rewrite
src/frontend/index.html no longer contains obvious mojibake or stale W4 contradictions
A focused guard exists to reduce false-positive deploy PASS risk for HTML body integrity/parity
Openclaw SIT deploy completes against the intended ref/SHA
Live runtime proof confirms both /phase2/prototype and /index.html behave correctly
Quick Export and Template Export runtime wiring still work after the fix
Final response clearly separates what is closed now from any non-blocking follow-up
final_instruction_to_copilot: Take this through to closure. Do the Git fix, strengthen the proof gate, redeploy through Openclaw, and verify the live runtime end to end. Do not stop at diagnosis, plan-only output, or source-marker evidence.
